evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: Clear, bounded UI action and inputs allow reasonable implementation estimation.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL
evaluations.rationale: Specific deliverable (shareable URL) is sufficiently scoped for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Well-scoped UI behaviour; possible edge cases but estimatable without detailed design.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Displays list of items for current session — clear scope for implementation effort.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item is a bounded interaction and can be reasonably estimated.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items to a list is specific enough to plan and estimate.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item is a concrete UI operation with estimatable effort.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item is a bounded behaviour that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Behaviour is defined (show immediately) and implementable without excessive ambiguity.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average is a concrete calculation and decision rule that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: have the "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Clear trigger and behavior; sufficiently specific for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Simple, concrete UI action with no broad ambiguity.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimation is a bounded behaviour; implementation effort is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Common, bounded integration task; while formats may be specified later, this is estimatable at a feature level.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Specific, limited interaction that can be estimated without detailed design.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games is a defined user action (listing/paging/search) and is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing/exporting a transcript is a concrete deliverable with estimatable scope.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Specific export format (HTML) and action allow for reasonable estimation.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: CSV export is a bounded implementation task and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game and associated data is a discrete operation estimatable in scope.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Account creation inputs and behaviour are well-defined and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Standard, well-scoped authentication behaviour is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Updating account details is a bounded feature that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Account deletion is a concrete operation; complexity is limited and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display behaviour is well-understood and estimatable despite implementation details.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminder via email is a standard, bounded feature and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: The choice of scoring sequences is concrete and implementable; effort to add options is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: A numeric limit is specified, making the scope bounded and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: User joining flow is clearly described and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Displaying the current item is a bounded UI task suitable for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: A list view of upcoming items is concrete and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Real-time indicator of who has given an estimate is specific enough to estimate (e.g., UI + signalling).

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Clear trigger and behaviour for showing estimates; bounded and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: be able to change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Well-defined rule for editability; estimatable implementation effort.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Displaying prior estimates is a defined data-display feature and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Explicit display requirement with bounded scope, allowing estimation.

evaluations.evidence: able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Timer duration and visibility are specific; implementation is estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Clear trigger and behaviour for reset; bounded and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling/back-navigation functionality is concrete and estimatable.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Deterministic card ordering is a specific requirement that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Edit rule is clear and bounded for implementation estimation.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: UI element (thumbnail) and placement are concrete enough for estimating work.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a measurable target and can be estimated at feature level.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Creating a definitions list is a bounded deliverable amenable to estimation.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: 'as fast as possible' is an unbounded/ambiguous acceptance criterion that prevents a reasonable implementation estimate.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Targeted browsers and versions are explicitly listed, making scope clear for estimation.

evaluations.evidence: site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Although the phrase 'where possible' is slightly subjective, the target (W3C guidelines) is concrete enough to estimate work at a feature level.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: The term 'respond quickly' is vague/unquantified, so implementation effort cannot be reasonably estimated without measurable criteria.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Supporting Unicode is a clear technical requirement and estimatable in scope.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: Although somewhat subjective, defining a sensible URL scheme is a bounded design task that can be estimated.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Designing error pages is a concrete UI task; 'nice' is subjective but does not prevent reasonable estimation.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: 'Non-identifiable' is ambiguous/legal/technical and may imply broad, complex anonymization requirements making estimation infeasible without clarification.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: The phrase 'some metrics' is underspecified (which metrics, granularity, retention), preventing a reliable implementation estimate.
